 1993 Brewers Racing Sausages getting restored for display in Madison
 MADISON, Wis. — The original Brewers Racing Sausages from 1993 are being restored and will be on display at the new Wisconsin History Center when it opens in December 2027.
The original costumes are being restored at the State Archive Preservation Facility in Madison.
The sausage races started virtual, played on the scoreboard. Then graphic designer Michael Dillon came up with the idea for live mascot racing, a first for the majors.
"They're doing the normal you know virtual scoreboard sausage race, and then when they get to County Stadium, out from the outfield wall comes three actual men in an Italian sausage, Polish sausage and a bratwurst suit," Director of Curatorial Services at the Wisconsin Historical Society, Leo Landis said.
Now there are five sausages. Hot dog and chorizo were added. The costumes stand more than seven feet tall.
"The three original sausages were a bratwurst, a Polish sausage, Italian sausage, and we've got Mr. Bratwurst right here. He really is comprised just of three materials: some fabric, some foam and hot glue," Landis said.
Conservators are studying the materials to restore the three original costumes.
"If we use an adhesive, we probably won't use hot glue. We will use something more museum-based that is easy to reverse," the conservator said.
The new history center is being built in Madison and will open at the end of 2027.
